title: How long is a Monday?
hook: A day has 24 hours. So why is it Monday somewhere for much longer than that?

knows: that the date changes at midnight
that different places are in different time zones
doesNotKnow: that a calendar date exists somewhere on Earth for far longer than 24 hours

misconception: Every calendar day exists everywhere for exactly 24 hours, as a single wall of midnight.
objective: The learner can explain that one date lasts 24 hours plus the spread of clock offsets (26 hours), so it exists somewhere for 50 hours.

claims.text: Clocks on Earth run from UTC-12 to UTC+14, a spread of 26 hours.
claims.source: IANA tz database: Pacific/Kiritimati is UTC+14; UTC-12 is the nominal offset for Baker and Howland Islands (uninhabited US territories; no IANA zone, listed as Etc/GMT+12). Wikipedia 'List of UTC offsets'. From memory, not checked online.

claims.text: Monday starts first on Kiritimati at Sunday 10:00 UTC and ends last on Baker Island at Tuesday 12:00 UTC.
claims.source: Local midnight at UTC+14 is 24 - 14 = 10:00 UTC the day before; local midnight ending Monday at UTC-12 is 48 + 12 = 60 h after Sunday 00:00 UTC, i.e. Tuesday 12:00 UTC. Computed in Demo.tsx from the offsets.

claims.text: One date exists somewhere on Earth for 24 + 26 = 50 hours.
claims.source: Arithmetic from c1: 60 - 10 = 50 hours, computed in Demo.tsx (MON_HOURS).

claims.text: The shaded bands are nominal 15-degree zones, not legal time zones; the two dots mark Kiritimati (about 1.9 N, 157.4 W) and Baker Island (about 0.2 N, 176.5 W).
claims.source: Nominal zones: offset n covers longitudes 15n +/- 7.5 degrees. Island coordinates from memory of a gazetteer (Kiritimati 1.87 N 157.36 W; Baker Island 0.19 N 176.48 W), not checked online. Neither island exists in the 1:110m shapes; drawn as markers. No border or date-line claims are drawn.

recall.question: If clocks on Earth only ran from UTC-10 to UTC+10, for how many hours would a date exist somewhere?
recall.why: A date lasts 24 hours in each place, and the places start it over a 20-hour spread, so it exists somewhere for 24 + 20 = 44 hours.
